title: Fish with Cream or White Sauce, Not Tuna or Lobster

content.title: About
content.content: This dish features tender white fish (such as cod, hake or sea bass) cooked in a light cream or white sauce made from broth, cream and aromatic herbs. The sauce adds a silky texture without overpowering the natural flavor of the fish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The creamy sauce is often based on fish stock, cream and white wine.
Preparing fish in a white sauce dates back to 18th‑century French cuisine.
The dish cooks quickly: fish is poached or baked for 5‑10 minutes, while the sauce thickens in 3‑4 minutes.
Lemon juice, dill, parsley or shallots are commonly added for extra aroma.
It can fit low‑fat diets when using reduced‑fat cream or substituting with yogurt.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: White fish provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Although lower than in fatty fish, it still contributes to cardiovascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The fish supplies B12, niacin and B6, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Selenium, phosphorus and iodine are present, important for thyroid health and immunity.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The gentle sauce makes the dish easy on the stomach, suitable for people with digestive sensitivities.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to fish and should avoid this dish.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Using a lot of broth or soy sauce can make the dish overly salty.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cream in the sauce may cause issues for lactose‑intolerant people; plant‑based creams are an alternative.

items.title: Food contaminants
items.content: Certain fish can contain heavy metals; purchase from reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, typically with boiled potatoes, rice or fresh vegetables. Garnish with chopped herbs and a lemon wedge.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked fish and sauce in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. It can be frozen for up to 1 month, though the sauce texture may change.
